status: Concept exploration only; no game or Blender modifications.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE polished 3D game environment concept sheet with six equal large panels in a clean 3-column by 2-row grid, landscape format. Each panel is a different SMALL maintenance / staff-only room behind a late-1990s shopping mall, for the liminal horror game Backrooms: Stay Quiet. This is exploratory concept art for buildable modular Blender rooms, NOT a real game screenshot.
Show each room from a human eye-level doorway view, wide enough to read the room and its exits. Cohesive restrained indie-game realism, clean readable geometry and silhouettes, moderate prop density, clear empty floor paths, a few grouped maintenance objects against walls. Small believable service spaces with low ceilings. Not huge halls, not tiny inaccessible closets. Relatable nostalgic mall back-of-house, slightly eerie but useful-looking. Broad simple wall geometry, believable worn materials; detail from fixtures and textures rather than thousands of objects.
Palette: faded beige painted block walls, dull mint/teal lower wall stripe, off-white ceiling panels, grey linoleum or small utility tiles; occasional muted orange doorframe and dark red utility labels. Fluorescent ceiling fixtures, slightly different cool/warm light by room, gently underlit far doors but readable exposure. Slightly worn, dusty, abandoned after closing; no extreme decay, no gore, no characters.
Panel 1 top left: JANITOR DEPOT. Beige cleaning trolley, compact old floor buffer, mop rack, shelves of paper rolls and detergent bottles, folded yellow caution sign. Dry floor. One doorway, useful short side-room.
Panel 2 top center: ELECTRICAL ROOM. Grey metal breaker cabinets, old analog meters, surface conduit and overhead cable tray. Two aligned usable doors make a straight shortcut, cabinets only along the side walls. Safe static closed equipment, no sparks.
Panel 3 top right: HVAC SERVICE. One large galvanized ventilation trunk along the wall and ceiling, accessible filter housing, modest pipe cluster and removable service panels. An obvious unobstructed route into a connected side service hallway; maintenance room with human-scale ceiling.
Panel 4 bottom left: REPAIR WORKSHOP. Worn workbench, vise, sparse pegboard of tools, small plastic parts drawers, old desk lamp, a removed escalator motor as one distinctive spare part on a low pallet. Clear central floor, one dark far doorway.
Panel 5 bottom center: MALL STORAGE. Shelved folded chairs, compact stacked boxes, rolled old carpet, detached colorful geometric mall wayfinding sign and stored party decorations, artificial plant. Two doors on opposite walls with clear passage. No wall of random junk.
Panel 6 bottom right: PA / CCTV ROOM. Small beige CRT surveillance monitor console showing indistinct empty mall corridors, VHS deck, cassette PA amplifier, telephone patch panels and a corded beige telephone. One rolling chair tucked in. A mint-coloured service door visible.
Place simple crisp numeric labels 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06 in the same small top-left position in each panel; NO other overlaid captions. Tiny in-world maintenance stickers can be indistinct; no brands or logos. Thin neutral gutters. All six panels equally important, legible and stylistically matched.
Constraints: NO water, no puddles, no aquarium, no fountain, no futuristic sci-fi, no luxury mansion, no floating holograms, no grass floors, no excessive clutter, no dramatic volumetric fog, no fisheye, no monsters. This should look practical to model as a small reusable Roblox environment kit with character and strong room identity.
